answer: Speaker C (User Interface Designer) wanted radio waves because they allow the remote control to work in any direction without tuning, as stated in IS1005a and IS1005b. Arguments against radio waves were cost and market expectations: Speaker B (Technical Designer) preferred infra-red due to lower price and sufficient range, and Speaker D (Marketing Expert) said spending extra money was not worth it since customers expect infra-red. The team chose infra-red signals for the remote control.

answer: In meeting c, Team IS1006 agreed to use a simple battery as the energy source instead of solar cells. In meeting d, they changed to a combined energy source using a hand dynamo mechanism plus a battery. The team reduced costs from their initial 17.8 Euro estimate by choosing simple push buttons instead of LCDs and opting for titanium design over rubber, which is more expensive, allowing budget space for speech recognition technology.
